solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Polish bishop not up to the job?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
someone not up to the job is lacking or deficient

explanation.surface: A Polish bishop is accused of being incompetent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be a nationality; it is the noun for shoe polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacking is a dark paste rubbed into boots and grates, a kind of polish.

clue.text: Look — animal has got caught! With this?

indicators.note: the animal is caught inside the word for look

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A cowboy points out that an animal has been snared.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition asks what the animal was caught with.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a roped noose thrown to catch cattle, the tool that captured it.

clue.text: Tube containing gift presented to sailor, something really good

parts.note: a Christmas cracker is a paper tube holding a small present
Jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is handed a gift-filled tube that turns out to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British party tube pulled apart with a bang to release a trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackerjack is informal for an excellent person or thing.

clue.text: Terribly Nimby — nothing all right, the way I see things

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly messed up

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A NIMBY objector says terribly little is acceptable, in their opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges NIMBY into INMYB. A NIMBY (not in my back yard) objects to local development.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in my opinion, a personal viewpoint.

clue.text: Using bits of news maybe to ascertain personal position

definitions.text: Using bits of news maybe to ascertain personal position

parts.words: Using bits of news maybe to ascertain personal position
parts.note: the letters N, E, W and S are compass points, bearings, so working out where one is uses them

explanation.walkthrough: The bits of news are its letters N, E, W, S: the compass points used to find direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means working out where you are, literally by compass, or figuratively in a new situation.

clue.text: Grumble about head, getting hold of doctor

indicators.note: the word for head grips the doctor's letters, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone complains about their headache and grabs a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to lament or complain about it, taking an object just as the definition does.

clue.text: Dull old boy turning up to join clique

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the letters backwards

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
a ring is a closed group

explanation.surface: A tedious former pupil arrives to join an exclusive set.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring means tedious, uninteresting.

clue.text: Bird unable to fly in ditch — time to get out of it

indicators.note: time leaving the ditch means its letter is removed

parts.note: a moat is a defensive ditch

explanation.surface: A flightless bird stuck in a ditch must eventually climb out.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a huge extinct flightless bird of New Zealand.

clue.text: Very painful, as in going mad

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going mad is described as excruciating.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonising means causing great pain or anguish.

clue.text: It's so mild — bees being this?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the weather is ..., so mild
bees in a swarm are ..., crowding about

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AS WARM for the first sense: 'so' is AS and 'mild' is WARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswarm means teeming or crowded, as bees are when they swarm; split in two it says the weather is as warm.

clue.text: Herb, sailor with tatty cloth on

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a rag is a scrap of worn cloth

explanation.surface: A sailor called Herb wears a scruffy garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name for the sailor; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary plant used in French cooking, an example of a herb.

clue.text: Century Kent's opener hit

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

indicators.note: the opening letter of the county's name is taken, like an opening batsman

explanation.surface: A Kent opening batsman hits a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county with a cricket side; a century is a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonk is British slang for striking hard, especially a cricket ball.

clue.text: Mad relations, possible cause of downfall

parts.note: going bananas means going mad
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Crazy relatives might bring someone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' suggests ruin, but here it is a literal slip and tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on a discarded fruit peel is the classic comic way to slip over, so it causes a literal fall.

clue.text: Corrupt MS — one copied unfortunately here?

indicators.note: unfortunately implies things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled
copied means the letter for one appears a second time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A manuscript was badly copied and corrupted at the place it was produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges CORRUPT, MS and II. 'Corrupt' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scriptorium was the monastery room where scribes copied manuscripts, the place meant by the definition.

clue.text: Deceitful financial documents after initial incentive

indicators.note: the documents come after the incentive in the answer

parts.note: a spur is the first prompt that urges something on
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: Dodgy paperwork follows an early inducement in a financial scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, and so deceptive in nature.

clue.text: Extravagance of academic American, one getting on

parts.note: prof is short for professor
US means American
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American professor is getting old and spending lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Profusion means great abundance, lavishness or excess.

clue.text: Member of Queen's family said to be agitated

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard, not written

parts.note: a royal is one of the monarch's relatives

explanation.surface: A royal is reported to be in a state of upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To roil is to churn or be stirred up, like troubled water or emotions.

clue.text: Maiden has spoken — spoken indistinctly

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
uttered means said or spoken

explanation.surface: A young woman has had her say, but mumbled it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to speak quietly and unclearly, under one's breath.

clue.text: Artist unknown in part of India

indicators.note: the unknown letter sits in the Indian state's name

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unidentified artist lives somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Ceremonial stuff, ultimately terrible joke taking time

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word terrible

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dreadful joke drags on during a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipage is the trappings and equipment of state, such as a carriage with attendants, used on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Cross crunchy bridge with bits falling off the sides

indicators.text: with bits falling off the sides
indicators.note: letters at both sides of the phrase are dropped, leaving the inner stretch

explanation.surface: A brittle bridge crumbles at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is a noun, a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different varieties, a cross.

clue.text: Wrong turning at the end of country dance

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes at the end of the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country

indicators.note: turning means the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone takes a wrong turn on the way to a country dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country dance' reads as one phrase, but 'country' is a wordplay piece and 'dance' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot was a ragtime-era ballroom dance, so it is a type of dance.

clue.text: Contact (not with the face) that was painful!

indicators.note: the face of the word is its front, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: touch is contact

explanation.surface: A blow that missed the face still hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation people utter when something hurts them.

clue.text: Cold meat free from contamination

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
lean is meat without fat

explanation.surface: Chilled meat is declared safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means pure, unpolluted and untainted.

clue.text: One looking after baby tries playing with it, ending with exhaustion

indicators.note: playing with the letters suggests rearranging them freely
the closing letter of the word exhaustion is taken

explanation.surface: A babysitter tries playing with the child until worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TRIES and IT into SITTERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter-in is someone who minds a child while its parents are out, a babysitter.

clue.text: Asian couple being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join

explanation.surface: An Asian pair are given a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tai are a group of peoples of Thailand, Laos and southern China, so a Tai is Asian.

clue.text: King wasn't well, had a complaint

parts.note: R is Rex, king
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A sickly king grumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a complaint' looks like illness, echoing 'wasn't well', but it means protested.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or protest angrily.

clue.text: A foreign character seen as savage

parts.note: un is French for a
kind means nature or character

explanation.surface: A foreign figure is regarded as brutal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkind means cruel or harsh, as a savage remark is.

clue.text: Deposit small amount of money, getting ecstatic about it

indicators.note: the word for ecstatic goes around the coin

parts.note: sent is old slang for enraptured
a dime is a ten-cent US coin

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to bank a little money.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit.
